text:
[IRET.28.0.1] **Goals.** The structure:

- **must** be a single data structure that every table of `[IRET.28.2]`
  uses.
- **must** centralize the probe, backward-shift delete, grow, and load
  machinery so the bug class is fixed in one tested place.
- **must** keep the hot path (the alpha join scan) a flat dense-array
  walk with no per-element indirection, and **must** keep probing
  cache-friendly.
- **must** be deterministic and bit-identical across runs and platforms
  (`[IRET.28.10]`, `[LDET.3.4]`). Its iteration order **must not** feed
  timetag assignment (`[LDET.5.5]`).
- **must** support pre-sizing and a grow-forbidden ("locked") mode for
  real-time use (`[IRET.28.11]`, [RTCT]).
- **must** be exhaustively property / fuzz / invariant tested
  (`[IRET.28.16]`).

idris.name: Iret_28_0_1__engine
idris.note: The engine under the reading 'iteration order feeds timetag assignment': dense memories and a counter-stamped agenda, for one rule `A a, B b`.

idris.name: iret_28_0_1__assert
idris.note: An assertion under the reading: left-activation iterates the B memory in dense order and stamps in that order; right-activation iterates the left memory as appended.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__dense_refuted
idris.note: Witnesses the goal's prohibition: an order fed by the dense iteration order depends on how the set was reached and fails [LDET.5.9] on a three-fact history. The timetag is a function of the match and of working memory, the key of [LDET.5.5], and Rete/NetworkOrderKeep.idr proves every history sorts by it.
